cells.tense: You're sitting with something you feel deeply, and you're letting it settle before you say or do anything about it.
cells.ask: offer a few quiet minutes to where this feeling is heading, letting it get deeper than it's been.
cells.core:
Something real is arriving in you and you're not rushing it. It comes in, it fills, it rests, and you can sit there without needing the next thing yet. The feeling gets to be what it actually is before you decide anything about it, and that's a steady place to stand. Nothing has to be forced through the door while you're still feeling your way around it.

Feelings that get this kind of quiet don't stay shallow. Let one of them take you further down than you'd normally go. Not to act on it, just to see how far it reaches and what it touches on the way down. What you find there usually outlasts whatever you'd have done with it in a hurry.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting the feeling arrive and settle before you do anything with it.
cells.verb: sitting still with what the heart already knows
cells.place: at the door where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: You're bracing for how this will land and how you'll be met, living in a version of it that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: set it down for a day and let what's already here be enough for now.
cells.core:
When this is working, you take what's arriving at face value. It comes in, you feel it, and you don't need to know yet what it'll become. That kind of welcome is what lets good things come near you at all, and it's why people bring you the real version of what's on their mind.

Right now you're already at the far end of it, tracking how it'll go, what it'll mean, whether it'll hold. The quiet you'd need to actually feel it is getting spent on the future. Let what's already grown sit a while longer, out there in the open where it can finish ripening. Not everything good gets picked the moment it's ripe, and the ones you pick early tend to taste like the wait you didn't give them.
cells.sheetLine: You're already living past what hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: sitting still with what the heart already knows
cells.place: at the door where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: You're still standing where something was handed to you, holding what it did or didn't mean instead of turning to what's here now.
cells.ask: let one thought you keep circling land somewhere, and see what that frees up.
cells.core:
Something new shows up and you meet it while it's still happening — that's the whole of it, no finding the right feeling first, just facing the door while it's open.

Something warm keeps trying to come in and it isn't getting through. You're still back at that other moment, waiting on a read that already happened. The door is open; you just haven't stepped through it. What's scattered in your head isn't a mess to muscle through. It's a few thoughts that need setting next to each other once, honestly, by you. Do that, and the thing you've been unable to feel can start moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You're still back at the door instead of standing in what's here.
cells.verb: sitting still with what the heart already knows
cells.place: at the door where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: You're quieter and more settled than you let on, and you're calling it just how you are instead of something you're doing.
cells.ask: name one judgment that came out of real thought and stop calling it a reflex.
cells.core:
Feelings come to rest in you and they stay, and you arrive there on purpose even if you've never called it that. It's what lets you stand near people without losing your own footing. It's also what they come to when they need somewhere calm to lay something down, and they can feel the difference between that and someone who's simply quiet.

Let one of the quieter things you know be seen as yours. Not the loud opinion — the deeper read, the one that took concentration and holds several things at once. Say it's yours out loud once, to yourself is fine.
cells.sheetLine: Your steadiness is work you're doing, and you call it nothing.
